analysis:
All three changed files are new test-only files (no production source) covering operator rollback (`darkbloom update --rollback`), the rollback plan and refusals, and journaled recovery. They add no runtime attack surface and change no threat-model assumptions. I found no regression.

UpdateRollbackEndToEndTests.swift runs the built CLI and enclave binaries, ad-hoc signed, in a UUID-named scratch directory under the realpath'd temp dir. It sets the child's HOME and CFFIXED_USER_HOME to a scratch directory and fakes the host (launchd, drain, restart, cluster check). The update check is pointed at a loopback 127.0.0.1 Hummingbird server on an ephemeral port (asserted >=49152). SelfUpdater is built with verifyCodeSignatures:false, and the coordinator URL is the discard port 9, so no real coordinator, launchd job or provider process is touched. The ad-hoc signing and disabled signature verification exist only in the test.

UpdateRollbackPlanTests.swift and UpdateRollbackRecoveryTests.swift use temp-dir fixtures and a loopback MockCoordinator. They test controls that support T-043, T-034 and T-054: predecessor hash-mismatch refusal, installNotRecorded when the live bundle was replaced out of band, busy refusal under the cross-process lease, and stale-plan refusal (changedSinceConfirmation). They also cover crash-boundary recovery under the lease, and that the quarantine holds for both auto-update paths, including a stale v2 watchdog.

Open questions for the next pass: the production rollback implementation (SelfUpdater.rollBackToPredecessor, UpdateRecoveryStore.rollback) is not in this batch. Whether the rollback to a retained predecessor re-verifies signature and qualification (T-054, A-017) in production, given the tests use verifyCodeSignatures:false, is therefore unverified here. A downgrade-attack surface (T-047-style stale or downgrade authority) also depends on that code and is not assessed.
